metadata.note: Knox and Lincoln Railroad and every later passenger operator on the Bath/Woolwich - Rockland corridor, Maine. One OSM trace (old_railway_operator=MEC, 'Rockland Branch', Brunswick - Rockland 56.6 mi) cut into: Woolwich - Rockland drawn twice on identical geometry (Rule 4 split at the 1891 Maine Central lease); Bath - Woolwich over the Carlton Bridge from 1927 only; Wiscasset - Newcastle for the Maine Coast Railroad's 1995 anchor; and Brunswick - Rockland for Maine Eastern (2004-2015) and Midcoast Railservice (2023). Brunswick - Bath for 1870-1959 belongs to the Kennebec & Portland / Maine Central Brunswick - Bath layer and is not redrawn here. Research: research/branches/knox_and_lincoln_railway.txt.
not_yet_sourced: Opening day: 31 Oct 1871 (Wikipedia K&L and Rockland Branch text) vs 30 Oct 1871 (Rockland Branch infobox). Same year; the cited Portland Daily Press of 1 Nov 1871 was not read directly.
Maine Central takeover: 1891 (three Wikipedia articles) vs 1890 (Maine Maritime Museum, Bath Freight Shed history). Split drawn at 1891.
Last Maine Central passenger train: 4 Apr 1959 (Wikipedia, citing the April 1959 Official Guide, not read) vs 1958 (abandonedrails.com). Drawn to 1959.
Rockland 1st station (MP 83.0, replaced 1886): location not found in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap; all K&L years are drawn to the 2nd station (MP 84.3).

Woolwich: the abandoned OSM grade (ways 253924822/821/820) taken as the pre-1927 ferry-slip approach is an unsourced geometric identification. Woolwich 1st (MP 37.0) -> 2nd (MP 37.1/37.2) station move falls between the 1911 and 1921 timetables; year and reason unknown.

Bath - Woolwich train ferry 1871-1927: not drawn (not rail). Whether through passengers rode in the cars or crossed on the passenger steamer, and whether the railroad or a 'People's Ferry Company' owned the boats, is unresolved.

Maine Central: Rockland Wharf (MP 84.3 - 84.9, 1921 [ANCHOR], Fowler letter b) is NOT drawn: the only rail toward the harbour in OSM is the 'Rockland Wharf Spur/Branch' (ways 171368729, 11453065, 11453055, 11453062), which leaves the yard west of the station and ends at a buffer stop at (-69.10504, 44.09781) in the South End, ~0.45 mi south of Tillson Avenue/Tillson Wharf, with ~1.2 mi of track against the documented 0.6 mi; OpenHistoricalMap has nothing. The 1921 wharf track could not be identified, so the anchor is omitted rather than drawn on the wrong track.
Maine Coast Railroad excursions: only 1995 is documented (magazine abstracts). First/last excursion years 1991-2000 and the Wiscasset - Warren / Wiscasset - Bath variants are unsourced.
Maine Eastern: first passenger date in 2004 not found; Brunswick boarding point before Maine Street Station not established.
Pen Bay Scenic Railroad (Midcoast Rail Heritage Trust over the Cumberland and Knox, planned 2026): no run documented as of 2026-10-13; not drawn.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; only the 1951 Maine Central running time (~2 h 30 min Brunswick - Rockland, partly illegible OCR) was measured.
metadata.freight_only: Not drawn (Rule 1): Rockland Branch 1959-2003 (except the 1995 anchor), 2016-2022 and 2024-present; the Rockland wharf/waterfront and South End trackage; lime-quarry and cement spurs at Rockland and Thomaston. The 2019 NNEPRA test run to Rockland carried officials, not the public, and the 2018 Amtrak pilot never ran.

Station sampling (trace mileage from Brunswick vs Maine Central timetable milepost minus Brunswick 27.6): Bath 8.66/8.7, Wiscasset 20.14/20.15, Newcastle 27.18/27.15, Waldoboro 38.77/38.6, Warren 45.39/45.35, Thomaston 52.16/52.5, Rockland 56.59/56.7. Bath, Wiscasset, Newcastle and Rockland are OSM station nodes; Waldoboro, Warren and Thomaston are hand pins placed on the MEC-tagged track (Nominatim was not trusted for Maine towns), so their sample is only as good as the pin. This feature: 46.61 mi from the Woolwich point described below to Rockland 2nd station, against the documented 47.3 mi Woolwich (1st, MP 37.0) - Rockland (MP 84.3) (Fowler; Feb 1952 Guide and 1955 MEC timetable agree to 0.1 mi). On the ferry-era route the start point sits at about MP 37.35, so the comparable documented figure is ~46.95 mi; the trace is within 0.35 mi of it. WOOLWICH END: the feature starts at (-69.79765, 43.91897), where an abandoned, unnamed OSM grade (ways 253924822, 253924821 - a footway tunnel under US 1 - and 253924820, ~0.4 mi) leaves the live line and runs down to the Kennebec bank ~500 m north of the Carlton Bridge. That grade is PROBABLY the pre-1927 approach to the Woolwich train-ferry slip and 1st station (MP 37.0); this identification is mine, from geometry alone, and is NOT sourced. Starting here keeps the feature off track that was most likely built for the 1927 bridge; the ferry-approach grade itself is not drawn, because the post-1927 Maine Central feature that shares this geometry did not use it. The ~1.3 mi from Bath station over the bridge to this point is drawn separately as 'Maine Central: Bath – Woolwich (Carlton Bridge)', 1927-1959. LATER ALIGNMENT AT ROCKLAND (Rule 2): the Rockland terminal moved in 1886 from the 1st station (MP 83.0) to the 2nd (MP 84.3) (Fowler: 'Rockland (1st)(rl.1886)'). Neither OSM nor OpenHistoricalMap shows the 1st station or a pre-1886 approach, so every year here is drawn to the 2nd station (Rockland Station, OSM node 13762069154 / buffer stop 101976310); for 1871-1886 the last ~1.3 mi overstates the line's reach, on an alignment that may itself differ from the original. No straight-line legs. The Rockland Wharf extension (MP 84.3-84.9) is not drawn: see metadata.

segments.note: Knox and Lincoln Railroad (Penobscot and Kennebec charter 1849; renamed Knox and Lincoln 1864) opened Woolwich - Rockland 31 Oct 1871 (Wikipedia K&L and Rockland Branch article text, citing the Portland Daily Press of 1 Nov 1871, p.3, which was not read directly; the Rockland Branch infobox says 30 Oct - same year). Every K&L station carries Fowler letter y (1876 Pathfinder Guide), the first primary confirmation of passenger service. Its own trains ran until the Maine Central lease of 1891 (three Wikipedia articles; the Maine Maritime Museum says 1890 - conflict recorded in metadata; split drawn at 1891). Bath was the real passenger terminal: cars crossed the Kennebec by train ferry to Woolwich until 1927, and that ferry is deliberately not drawn. The terminal at Rockland moved 1.3 mi in 1886; this segment is drawn to the 2nd station throughout (see geometry_quality). Stations: Woolwich, Nequasset, Montsweag, Wiscasset, Newcastle, Damariscotta Mills, Nobleboro, Winslow's Mills, Waldoboro, Warren, Thomaston, Rockland. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (about three trains a day assumed); no K&L frequency was sourced.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note names the sources for its dates (Wikipedia K&L and Rockland Branch for the Oct 1871 opening and the 1891 lease; branchline.uk Maine line 5, letter y, for 1876 timetable presence), as established in research/branches/knox_and_lincoln_railway.txt. The Portland Daily Press of 1 Nov 1871 is cited at second hand only. The headway is not sourced.

segments.note: Maine Central leased the Knox and Lincoln in 1891 (Wikipedia K&L, Rockland Branch and Rockland station; the Maine Maritime Museum says 1890 - conflict recorded in metadata) and bought it outright 20 Feb 1901, which did not change who ran the trains; nor did Boston & Maine joint management 1933-1955. Passenger service is confirmed across the era by Fowler letters z (1892/94), a (1911), b (1921), c (1932) and d (1954) on Wiscasset, Damariscotta Mills, Nobleboro, Winslow's Mills, Waldoboro, Warren, Thomaston and Rockland; by the Feb 1952 Official Guide, MEC Table 5 (times at Bath, Damariscotta Mills, Waldoboro, Thomaston and Rockland; through coaches Rockland - Portland and a De luxe Streamline Coach Rockland - Boston); and by the MEC public timetable of 30 Oct 1955, Table 4 'Rockland Branch', with times at every station. Last regularly scheduled passenger train 4 April 1959 (Wikipedia Rockland Branch and Rockland station, citing the April 1959 Official Guide); abandonedrails.com says 1958 (conflict recorded; 1959 is the better-sourced date). Until 1927 the cars crossed the Kennebec from Bath by train ferry (not drawn); from 24 Oct 1927 over the Carlton Bridge, drawn as its own feature. Freight continued after April 1959 (MEC, then Guilford) until the line fell out of use; the State of Maine bought it in 1987. Not drawn after 1959 (Rule 1). headway_min is an ESTIMATE ('three trains a day except Sunday' until 1958, per Wikipedia's Rockland station article; earlier frequencies not sourced).

The April 1959 Official Guide is cited via Wikipedia, not read. The headway is only loosely sourced.

The extra ~0.5 mi beyond Woolwich station is deliberate: it is the stretch most likely built in 1927 for the bridge approach, which the 1871-1959 Woolwich - Rockland features therefore leave off (see their geometry_quality; the ferry-grade identification is unsourced). 0.8 mi from Bath falls at about (-69.79875, 43.91261), just east of the bridge. The bridge itself is a single straight span in the simplified trace, which is real (a lift bridge), not an approximation. No straight-line legs. Nothing is drawn across the Kennebec before 1927: the train ferry is deliberately omitted.

segments.note: Rail traffic moved from the Bath - Woolwich train ferry to the new Carlton Bridge on 24 Oct 1927; the first passenger train over it was an excursion from Rockland carrying the Governor and Senator Frank W. Carlton (Press Herald 'Remember When', 2 Mar 2018). Before that there was no rail across the Kennebec, so this feature starts in 1927. Times at both Bath and Woolwich appear in the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 5) and the 30 Oct 1955 MEC timetable (Woolwich 37.1). Ended with the Rockland Branch's last passenger train, 4 April 1959 (Wikipedia Rockland Branch). headway_min is an ESTIMATE, as for the Rockland Branch.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Single proven year. Maine Coast Railroad (a Massachusetts Central affiliate) operated the state-owned line from 26 Oct 1990 until it lost the lease on 4 Dec 2000 (Wikipedia), but the only dated evidence of passenger excursions is two July 1995 magazine abstracts: Down East, 1 July 1995 ('fourteen-mile round-trips between Wiscasset and Newcastle') and Maine Times, 28 July 1995 ('runs excursion trains from Wiscasset to Newcastle'). Excursions almost certainly ran in other years between 1991 and 2000, but no other year is confirmed: do NOT widen this anchor without evidence, and do not delete it. Announced 1995 extras (a Wiscasset - Brunswick NAS air-show shuttle, foliage runs on the Brunswick - Augusta line) and the undated Wiscasset - Warren / Wiscasset - Bath variants are not drawn. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (at most about one excursion a day assumed).

segments.note: Maine Eastern Railroad (a Morristown & Erie subsidiary) took over the state-owned line on 1 Nov 2003 (one source) or 1 Jan 2004 (Railway Age); passenger trains 'resumed running on the Rockland line in 2004' (Bangor Daily News, 18 Jun 2013), and Wikipedia has ex-Amtrak F40PHs running the 2004 season. No first-run date was found and no 2003 passenger run is evidenced, so drawn from 2004. Seasonal (summer/fall) excursions Brunswick - Bath - Wiscasset - Newcastle - Rockland with ex-New Haven FL9s and streamlined coaches, connecting with the Amtrak Downeaster at Brunswick in 2014; ridership peaked near 19,000 in 2008; cut from two round trips a day to one in 2013 (BDN). 2014 added the 'Wiscasset Flyer' shuttles Wiscasset - Newcastle and Wiscasset - Bath (Boothbay Register 11 Jun 2014), on track already in this feature. Last season 2015: first trip 30 July 2015, weekends in August and October (BDN 28 Jan 2015); MaineDOT chose CMQ to run the line from 1 Jan 2016, and the midcoast 'haven't seen a passenger train since 2015' (BDN 10 Aug 2023). Where Maine Eastern trains boarded at Brunswick before Maine Street Station opened is not established; drawn from Maine Street Station throughout. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one to two seasonal round trips a day; ignores the off-season).

segments.note: A genuine one-season service, not an anchor. Midcoast Railservice (a Finger Lakes Railway subsidiary), with MaineDOT, ran 'a couple dozen excursions with stops between Brunswick and Rockland, including Bath, Wiscasset and Newcastle' (Bangor Daily News 12 Dec 2023) with one 76-seat RDC-type car: first public trips 4-6 Aug 2023 for the Maine Lobster Festival, short runs from Rockland toward Thomaston/Warren (Lincoln County News 29 Jun 2023, plan; BDN 12 Dec 2023, happened); Wiscasset - Bath trips 26 Aug 2023 (Wiscasset Newspaper 27 Aug 2023); last trip 8 Oct 2023 for the Damariscotta Pumpkin Festival, after which the car failed and could not be repaired. No trips found in 2024 or 2025; Midcoast gave up the lease in 2024. Drawn Brunswick - Rockland as the extent the BDN names; individual trips covered only parts of it. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (occasional excursion days only).
